video_metadata.working_title: MICHIGAN 1987 Cold Case Solved After 26 Years — Justice for Rick & Gail Brink
video_metadata.topic_one_sentence: Rick Brink, 28, and his wife Gail, 22, married about 18 months, were shot to death at their Park Township ranch house near Holland, Michigan, in November 1987; in January 2013 Gail's brother Ryan Wyngarden was arrested after his wife told cold-case detectives he had admitted the killings, and in 2014 a jury convicted him of two counts of first-degree premeditated murder.
video_metadata.primary_emotion_to_evoke: betrayal inside a family; grief stretched over 26 years; quiet respect for the detectives who reread the file

protagonist._instructions: The main character of your story - can be hero, villain, or antihero. Fill with verified facts only.
protagonist.age_at_time_of_events: Not verified in available sources; described as having had 'sexual encounters' with his sister when both were teenagers (police/prosecution claim). Age deliberately not stated in the script.
protagonist.occupation_or_status: Gail Brink's brother; in 2013 described as a Zeeland (Ottawa County) man; since 2014 serving two life sentences without parole; in the federal habeas record he was confined at the Thumb Correctional Facility, Lapeer, Michigan.
protagonist.location: Holland / Zeeland area, Ottawa County, Michigan
protagonist.background_brief: Interviewed within days of the 1987 killings and not considered a suspect; his alibi (doing laundry and babysitting at a friend's home with his then-girlfriend Pam Maracchini) was confirmed by her. He later married Pam. Arrested January 2013, convicted March 28, 2014, sentenced April 21, 2014. Maintains his innocence. [1][10][5][13]
protagonist.psychological_profile: Only documented behaviour: prosecutors and police said he was jealous of the couple's success and wanted to keep secret sexual encounters he and his sister had as teenagers [4][6]; at sentencing he spoke for more than an hour, criticised investigators and called the judge a liar [13][24].
protagonist.mundane_humanizing_detail: His 1987 alibi was an ordinary chore: doing laundry and babysitting at a friend's house [10][1].

victims_or_targets._instructions: People affected by the protagonist's actions. Include 3-5 key figures minimum.

individuals.name: Gail Brink (née Wyngarden)
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Shot to death; found lying on the couple's waterbed on Monday, November 23, 1987 [3][23]
individuals.humanizing_detail: Married to Rick about 18 months; the couple had only recently bought their ranch house in Park Township [3]

individuals.name: Rick Brink
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Shot twice in the head; found in the driver's seat of his Chevy Blazer in the driveway [14][23]
individuals.humanizing_detail: Failure to show up for work on Monday morning raised the alarm [3]

individuals.name: Budd Brink (spelling varies: Bud/Budd)
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Holidays and shared family times 'wiped away' by Ryan's anger and jealousy, per his sentencing statement (paraphrase) [24]
individuals.humanizing_detail: Asked the judge for the life sentence; recalled the priest's words at the funeral [24]
individuals.any_quotes_from_them: Recounted the priest's words: "This is not the work of the Lord, this is the work of the Devil." [24]

individuals.name: Pam Wyngarden (née Maracchini)
individuals.role_or_profession: Ryan's girlfriend in 1987, later his wife
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Gave the 1987 alibi; decades later told detectives Ryan admitted the killings and had taken her to the house, where she saw Gail, before the bodies were discovered [10][8]
individuals.humanizing_detail: The defence argued she was manipulated by police; appeals courts rejected that [18][17]

collective_victims_if_applicable.range_of_impacts: 26 years without answers; a killer inside the family circle at holidays [24]

characters.role_in_story: Ottawa County Sheriff's Office cold case detective
characters.key_actions_they_took: From 2011, with Det. David Blakely, reread thousands of documents, conducted 200+ interviews across state lines, spotted a discrepancy in interview transcripts and re-interviewed Pam [10][5]

characters.name: Daryl Cain
characters.key_actions_they_took: Testified that Ryan admitted to him in jail that he murdered his sister and her husband [2]

characters.name: David Hall
characters.role_in_story: Defence attorney at the preliminary examination

characters.name: Judge Jon Hulsing
characters.key_actions_they_took: Imposed two life sentences without parole on April 21, 2014; warned Ryan during his statement [24][25]

characters.name: Dr. Deborah Davis
characters.role_in_story: Proposed defence expert on memory and interrogation
characters.key_actions_they_took: Trial judge did not allow her to testify about interrogation techniques as used on Pam; this became an appellate/habeas claim [27]
characters.notable_quotes: Presentation title: 'Memory on Trial: Clues to Witness Accuracy' [27]

characters.name: Judge Arthur J. Tarnow
characters.key_actions_they_took: Denied Ryan's federal habeas petition (No. 2:18-cv-13390) and granted a certificate of appealability [27]

chronological_timeline._instructions: List every significant event with exact dates when possible. This is the backbone of your script.

events.what_happened: Rick and Gail marry (about 18 months before their deaths)
The couple had only recently bought a ranch house

events.date: Saturday, November 21, 1987 (reported date of the killings)
events.what_happened: Rick and Gail are shot to death with a .22-caliber pistol; reported that they had been at a wedding that evening (NOT verified in retrieved sources)
events.source: Date per case brief and Fox 17 (which misprints 'Saturday, Nov. 23') [10]; weapon type [5][10]

events.what_happened: Ryan and girlfriend Pam Maracchini later say they were doing laundry and babysitting at a friend's home
Per Pam's 2014 testimony, Ryan admitted the killings to her, took her to the house, grabbed her wrists and walked her to the bedroom, where she saw Gail
Couple fail to show up at their jobs; alarm raised; Rick found in driver's seat of his Chevy Blazer in the driveway, shot twice in the head; Gail found on the waterbed, shot
Ryan interviewed; not considered a suspect; alibi confirmed by Pam
Thanksgiving Day, three days after the discovery (calendar fact)
Cold case team created
Detectives Venus Repper and David Blakely assigned the Brink case; read thousands of documents; 200+ interviews, some across state lines
After noticing a discrepancy in transcripts, detectives re-interview Pam, who says Ryan told her he killed the Brinks
Ryan Wyngarden arrested and charged with two counts of first-degree premeditated murder
Preliminary examination; Pam testifies he admitted the killings; defence attorney David Hall calls some testimony hearsay; Ryan bound over for trial; secret relationship allegation aired

Trial; Pam is key witness; jailhouse informant Daryl Cain testifies; defence highlights discrepancies; Ryan testifies; memory expert Dr. Deborah Davis barred from testifying on interrogation techniques
Closing arguments
Jury convicts on two counts of first-degree premeditated murder after about four hours of deliberation
Judge Jon Hulsing imposes two life sentences without parole; Ryan speaks more than an hour, maintains innocence, calls judge a liar; Budd Brink's statement
Conviction upheld; court found no errors warranting reversal; defence had argued wife was manipulated by police

events.location: Michigan Court of Appeals / Michigan Supreme Court
events.what_happened: Post-conviction motion (relief from judgment) rejected by Ottawa circuit court, Court of Appeals (No. 339743) and Michigan Supreme Court; AP: 'three courts have rejected the effort'
Federal habeas petition No. 2:18-cv-13390 denied with prejudice by Judge Arthur Tarnow; certificate of appealability granted
events.significance: Federal review lost; any Sixth Circuit result not found

events.what_happened: No report found of release, retrial or reversal; he is presumed still serving life without parole (verify MDOC OTIS)

cold_open_material._instructions: The most dramatic moment of your story - this will be your hook.

the_moment.exact_location: Brink ranch house, Park Township, Ottawa County, Michigan
the_moment.what_is_happening: Two young people miss work; family drive to the house; Rick is in his Blazer in the driveway; Gail is inside on the waterbed
the_moment.what_makes_it_shocking: A newly married couple executed in a quiet lakeshore township three days before Thanksgiving
the_moment.ironic_twist: According to his wife's testimony, the killer had already shown her the scene before anyone found it, and she gave him his alibi.

cold_open_material.central_mystery_question: Who would kill a young couple who had just bought their first house, and why did it take 25 years for anyone to say his name?

the_method._instructions: How did the protagonist do what they did? Technical details that can be explained to a general audience.
the_method.technique_name: Cold-case file review and re-interview (no DNA or genealogy). A fingerprint is mentioned in the case request but NOT found in any retrieved source.
step_by_step_explanation: read thousands of documents, compare old transcripts
notice a discrepancy in an interview transcript
re-interview the alibi witness, now married to the man she alibied
jailhouse informant adds an alleged admission
the_method.why_it_worked: Relationships change over 25 years; the alibi was a single witness; transcripts preserved the original story so differences could be seen.

technical_terms_to_explain.simple_explanation: Someone's account that a person was somewhere else when a crime happened; only as strong as the person who confirms it.
Repeating in court what someone else said outside court; the defence argued some testimony was hearsay.
Killing planned in advance; carries mandatory life without parole in Michigan.
Michigan's post-appeal request to reopen a conviction.
A federal court review of whether a state conviction violated the Constitution.

the_method.scale_of_operation: Thousands of documents; more than 200 interviews [10]

systemic_failure._instructions: What institution, system, or authority failed to prevent this?
systemic_failure.how_they_were_supposed_to_protect: Test every alibi of people close to the victims
systemic_failure.why_they_failed: Ryan's alibi rested on one witness, his girlfriend; he was not considered a suspect [1][10]
specific_incompetence_examples: Alibi accepted from a single interested witness [10]
Case unsolved ~22 years before a dedicated cold case team existed (2009) [10]
systemic_failure.ironic_details_about_the_failure: The discrepancy that reopened the case was in the investigators' own transcripts [10].

the_investigation.investigating_agency: Ottawa County Sheriff's Office cold case team
the_investigation.initial_wrong_assumptions: That the brother was not a suspect and the alibi was solid [1]
the_investigation.key_breakthrough: Re-interview of Pam Wyngarden after a transcript discrepancy [10]
the_investigation.the_fatal_mistake: Confiding in, and taking to the scene, the one person who later testified against him (per her testimony) [8]
the_investigation.how_long_until_caught: About 25 years and 2 months (Nov 1987 to Jan 2013)

the_confrontation._instructions: The arrest, raid, or climactic moment when everything collapses.
the_confrontation.scene_description: Arrest and charge on two counts of first-degree premeditated murder [1][11]
the_confrontation.ironic_or_absurd_details: At sentencing he called the judge a liar [13][24]

charges_filed: Two counts of first-degree premeditated murder
legal_resolution.trial_date_if_applicable: March 2014, Ottawa County Circuit Court; verdict March 28, 2014
legal_resolution.notable_court_testimony: Pam: Ryan admitted the killings and took her to the house before discovery; motive included not wanting his sister to reveal their teenage sexual relationship [6][8]. Daryl Cain: jail admission [2]. Ryan took the stand (Holland Sentinel headline).

victim_impact_statements.key_quote: Recounted the priest's words: "This is not the work of the Lord, this is the work of the Devil."
victim_impact_statements.emotional_impact: Said holidays and shared times had been wiped away by Ryan's anger and jealousy (paraphrase) [24]

legal_resolution.protagonist_statement_in_court: Spoke for more than an hour, criticised investigators, maintained innocence; said "You're lying now, you are flat out lying." [13][24]
legal_resolution.current_status: Serving life without parole; direct appeal lost (2015); post-conviction bid rejected by three courts (2018); federal habeas denied (E.D. Mich.). No release or reversal found as of October 2026.

universal_stakes.why_this_matters_to_viewer: Most killers are known to their victims; the answer can sit at the family table for decades.
universal_stakes.how_this_could_happen_to_them: An alibi from one loyal person can bury the truth.
universal_stakes.lesson_or_warning: Secrets do not stay buried; witnesses change, and old files can be read again.
universal_stakes.current_relevance: Cold case teams across the US now reread files and re-interview witnesses.
